Famous for her many husbands, love of diamonds and her AIDS fundraising, the actress who won two film Oscars and was awarded an honorary Oscar for her humanitarian work, is celebrated by Liza Minnelli, Joan Collins, Pierce Brosnan, Angela Lansbury, Sir David Frost, Larry King, Robert Hardy, Barry Norman and Richard Burton's nephew Guy Masterson.

programme.title: The Hunt for Lady Olive and the German Submarine
programme.desc: A great maritime mystery lies deep beneath the waters of the Channel Islands. On the morning of 19 February 1917, German submarine UC-18 opened fire on Royal Navy Q-ship the Lady Olive. As the U-boat drew near to assess the damage it had inflicted, the Lady Olive counter-attacked. Both vessels were said to have sunk. For decades, divers and historians have searched to discover their fate and understand the fascinating story that led to this encounter, but no-one has come close to finding the wrecks. The documentary follows film-maker Karl Taylor and his specialist team over four years as they search to discover what happened on that fateful February day in 1917. Principal underwater photography: Karl Taylor and Peter Frankland.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson travels to Johnshaven, a once-important Scottish fishing village. When its skilled sailors were press-ganged into the Royal Navy in the late 18th century, it had to diversify into the flax and jute trade - which fed into the jute capital, the nearby city of Dundee. Ben discovers the ruins of an old cloth mill used to make cloth for sails and later coarse linen sacking, a product vital for transporting goods, and tries to solve the village mystery of what a circular building in a local’s garden could have been.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Peggy Sue Gerron Rackham, the inspiration behind Buddy Holly's famous song, is taken back by Arena to Lubbock, Texas, where she went to the same high school as Holly and where her marriage to his drummer Jerry Allison inspired a second tribute, Peggy Sue Got Married. She tells how both songs came to be written and provides some fresh insights into Buddy Holly's tragically short career. Among the other people recalling this era is Peggy Sue's neighbour Donna Fox, who also inspired a 1950s classic, Ritchie Valens's Donna.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Despite having come down in the world, Audrey feels appearances demand she take a holiday but dreads leaving her beloved Grantleigh Manor in DeVere's hands. So she picks the only safe week - when DeVere himself is on holiday.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth decides to have a second attempt at finding a small weekend home in the country and Elizabeth is called in to help her on her property search. But it quickly becomes clear Hyacinth and Richard have different views on the meaning of the word 'small'.

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin
programme.desc: When Reginald Perrin set out for work on Tuesday morning, he had no intention of calling his mother-in-law a hippopotamus. But he did, and from then on everything began to change.

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin
programme.desc: Reggie Perrin needs a month's holiday, but all he gets is an afternoon in a safari park with his wife, daughter, son-in-law and their two 'tiny adults'.

programme.title: Steve Backshall's Extreme Mountain Challenge
programme.desc: Adventurer and naturalist Steve Backshall embarks on one of the most dramatic and dangerous expeditions ever filmed by a BBC crew. His mission: to explore Venezuela's tepuis - ancient, sheer-sided mountains, lost worlds cut off from the jungle below. The second episode picks up where episode one left off with Steve and the climbing team halfway up the unclimbed, sheer-sided face of a remote tepui, about to make one last desperate attempt to reach the summit. It is then on to a new tepui and the second stage of the expedition. Joining up with a team of elite Italian cavers, Steve ventures deep within a tepui - inside a newly discovered cave. Within this dark underworld, the team encounter strange creatures, ancient mysteries and the raw geological forces that give the tepuis their unique shape. But nothing can prepare them for an attempt to forge a path into unexplored areas of the cave - a dangerous mission of intense claustrophobia and nerve-shredding tension. And then to end the adventure, Steve reunites with the climbing team for a spectacular finale: an epic abseil alongside the Angel Falls - the highest waterfall on earth.

programme.title: Elizabeth Taylor: A Tribute
programme.desc: Friends, family and co-stars share their memories of Elizabeth Taylor, the Hollywood icon. Famous for her many husbands, love of diamonds and her AIDS fundraising, the actress who won two film Oscars and was awarded an honorary Oscar for her humanitarian work, is celebrated by Liza Minnelli, Joan Collins, Pierce Brosnan, Angela Lansbury, Sir David Frost, Larry King, Robert Hardy, Barry Norman and Richard Burton's nephew Guy Masterson.

programme.title: The Secret Rules of Modern Living: Algorithms
programme.desc: Without us noticing, modern life has been taken over. Algorithms run everything from search engines on the internet to satnavs and credit card data security - they even help us travel the world, find love and save lives. Mathematician Professor Marcus du Sautoy demystifies the hidden world of algorithms. By showing us some of the algorithms most essential to our lives, he reveals where these 2,000-year-old problem-solvers came from, how they work, what they have achieved and how they are now so advanced they can even programme themselves.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Described as 'a long journey backwards to go forwards', Selina Thompson’s one-woman show Salt premiered in 2016. It quickly garnered awards and international success, and in 2021 it was adapted for TV - part drama, part documentary. Selina tells us about the background to the piece and the adaptations needed to create something for television that retained the power of the stage play. She discusses the influences behind the show and the need to engage the audience as part of the ritual. She also relates the consequences of performing something so physically and emotionally draining and the influence it had on the work that followed. And she talks about the continuing power the play still has - its themes and story as relevant now as ever.

programme.title: Salt by Selina Thompson

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Stephen Tompkinson looks back on his role in the BBC's 1994 adaptation of the acclaimed Terence Rattigan play The Deep Blue Sea, directed by pioneer of British film Karel Reisz - best known for Friday Night, Saturday Morning - and also starring Colin Firth, Ian Holm and Penelope Wilton. At the time, Stephen was making a name for himself in the popular comedy Drop the Dead Donkey, but here he explains why he seized the opportunity to join the cast, recalls the challenges involved and describes in particular what it was like to witness in person Penelope Wilton's central performance as Hester, described by critics as one of the decade's greatest acting masterclasses.

programme.title: Streets of Gold: Mumbai
programme.desc: Indian weddings normally take place over several days, and as part of his wedding preparations, Nikhil is preparing his ceremony of haldi - Hindi for turmeric. A turmeric paste is smeared on the groom by the women in his family. The ceremony signifies purity, prosperity and fertility. Nikhil and his bride-to-be Prarthana's wedding is a £30,000 extravaganza financed solely by the groom. With the main rituals completed, it's time for the Marathi tradition, in which the bride's family can demand a ransom to release her. 'We want cash!', shout the bridesmaids. The business of love is booming in Mumbai. Derby Day is an annual event at the iconic Mahalaxmi Racecourse in Mumbai. It is India's most glamorous horse race and combines high-society fashion, food, music and elite thoroughbred racing. We learn that Anupam Mittal, the entrepreneur, has skin in the game, and his horse Democracy is one of the favourites for a race in this year's Indian Derby weekend. However, it's not a good day for Democracy - she comes second to last. But it's a better day for Aradhana, the former air steward and aspiring actress from Delhi who lands a job cohosting online TV coverage of the Derby.

programme.title: Abandoned: Searching for Soldier Dad
programme.desc: DNA detectives track down the British soldiers who fathered children in Kenya then disappeared, leaving the children and their mothers without support. It's a quest to find a missing part of the children's identities. With access to every stage of this cutting-edge process, we follow as a team of lawyers and a leading geneticist travel to Kenya to help locate the British soldiers who fathered children then vanished. We witness the groundbreaking legal and scientific detective work used to find the missing dads. Lawyers believe British soldiers stationed at the army base in Nanyuki, Kenya, may have fathered hundreds of children over decades - the oldest we meet is now 70, the youngest just 18 months old. What's at stake is more than the reputation of the British army and the UK's post-colonial legacy. The mixed-heritage children have in some cases been ostracised by their communities and denied a chance of British citizenship since birth - something which could transform their lives.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: In 1964, a group of seven-year-olds appeared in a TV documentary about class in Britain. The cameras returned every seven years to see how their lives had changed. Now, more than 60 years later, 70 Up brings the project to an end. Jo Clinton-Davis, controller of factual at ITV, talks about the people who took part and the legacy of a remarkable TV experiment. Culture secretary Lisa Nandy has given an interview to Katie Razzall and The Media Show. She talks about BBC funding and cuts, its place in the UK media landscape, and proposals for a UK streaming service and a public service algorithm. Jake Kanter, international investigations editor at Deadline, gives his reaction. Channel 4’s undercover investigation into Reform UK has raised questions about how undercover journalism works and how political parties use opinion polls that later appear in the media. Sir John Curtice, Professor of politics at the University of Strathclyde, and Stephan Shakespeare, CEO of YouGov, consider the issues raised by the story.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: It's a landmark year for Poland's Baltic coast as the maritime city of Gdynia celebrates its 100th birthday. Gdynia sits on a stretch of coastline some call the Polish Riviera, and it's become increasingly popular as some holidaymakers search for less crowded and cooler alternatives to the hot and busy Mediterranean resorts. Reece Parkinson meets a new generation drawn to the maritime traditions of Gdynia, sees the remarkable revival of Gdańsk's shipyards and experiences the wild windswept beaches of the Hel Peninsula.

Memories of a family heirloom stop David in his tracks when he spots a figure of a lobster fisherman, but ceramics specialist Serhat is not convinced it will make a profit at auction. Across the fair, the blue team think about snapping up an early 1900s Japanese dragon-design photo frame – but will it fire up the bidders in the saleroom? With their shopping bags full, the teams head to Chichester to sell their items. A striking piece of jewellery impresses auctioneer Nick Hall, who takes to the rostrum to hammer out the best prices for the teams, but who will come out on top?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Auctioneer JB and restorer Robin travel to Edinburgh to meet three siblings who are facing the emotional task of selling their late mother's belongings. After a courageous battle with cancer, Joan passed away in 2023, leaving a remarkable collection and 17 heartfelt letters for her extended family. In those to her children, she urged them to dispose of her possessions with care. The auction proceeds will fund future family memories that Joan would approve of, including a long-planned trip to the USA. JB has one day to sift through a collection that took decades to assemble. He uncovers a treasure trove of jewellery, porcelain and model cars. Most excitingly, he uncovers a book containing signatures by The Beatles. Meanwhile, Robin transforms an old wheelbarrow and a charming wooden egg box. He also restores a Second World War helmet to its former glory. On auction day, JB wields the gavel, but can he raise enough cash to get the family to America?

programme.title: Mary at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: Dame Mary Berry takes a fond look back at her career in food while bringing viewers incredible mouth-watering recipes to try at home. Mary can trace her passion for outdoor cooking back 80 years, when she became a Girl Guide. Her friend, comedian Tom Allen, shares her love of the countryside but perhaps not the same aptitude for cooking. Together, they take a leisurely boat ride, sharing tales and facing the odd challenge as Tom attempts to drive the boat and navigate a lock. They stop along the way to cook Mary’s classic pan-fried cod, which she learnt to make at college, and the star dessert of Mary’s childhood, bread and butter pudding using her mother’s recipe, which she still loves eating anywhere. Mary also makes her brand new Thai chicken traybake and a reinvention of her 1970s cottage pie with a modern mash. Spending time with Tom is a chance for Mary to share some rarely seen TV archive footage of her early attempts at outdoor cooking, showing how much things have changed. It’s a moment to reflect that there are some recipes she still makes 70 years later and others that are brand new, inspired by Mary’s endless passion for home cooking.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp, experts Danny Sebastian and John Cameron and the teams go antique-hunting in Hele, before heading to Honiton for today’s auction. Natasha asks the Exeter public about a unique mystery item.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Just Mercy
programme.desc: Based on the true story of young lawyer Bryan Stevenson (Michael B Jordan) and his history-making battle for justice. After graduating from Harvard, Bryan might have had his pick of lucrative jobs. Instead, he heads to Alabama to defend those wrongly condemned, with the support of local advocate Eva Ansley (Brie Larson). One of his first, and most incendiary, cases is that of Walter McMillian (Jamie Foxx), who, in 1987, was sentenced to die for the notorious murder of an 18-year-old girl, despite a preponderance of evidence proving his innocence and the fact that the only testimony against him came from a criminal with a motive to lie. In the years that follow, Bryan becomes embroiled in a labyrinth of legal and political manoeuvrings and overt and unabashed racism as he fights for Walter and others like him - with the odds and the system stacked against them.

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk travels the world, heading down caves and up mountains in her search for mankind’s first moments. With the help of a variety of experts, she explains how the earliest societies were formed: from the easier ones to spell, like Rome and Greece, to the ones that are harder to spell, like Egypt and Mesopotamia.

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk tells the story of the birth of two of the world’s great religions and learns what came next: the fall of the Roman Empire, the Dark Ages, the Crusades and Genghis Khan. So a bit of a rough patch for mankind, if we’re honest. Along the way, Philomena asks experts hard-hitting questions about humanity’s progress and stands on or near impressive old ruins and inside museums, before the shot cuts away to some archive footage of the bits that don’t exist anymore or were too expensive to film at.

It's time for Mrs Brown to exercise all her diplomatic skills, starting with 'accidentally' letting Maria know all about Dermot's best man decision.

programme.title: Vigil
programme.desc: In the wake of the hub invasion, Henrik and Kirsten close in on the missing scientist, with Amy not far behind. As tensions rise and new allegiances are formed, the danger of Svalbard’s wilderness becomes apparent when a storm closes in. Our detectives must race to stop those with ulterior motives before it is too late, but will their relationship survive this newest hurdle?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Flo Headlam travel to Cambridge to help mum Louise and her two student children, Jacob and Maisie, transform their tired, lifeless garden into a space that brings them back together. The garden has become a forgotten patch that has lots of potential but is at the moment lacking character and structure. Louise, a full-time working mum, sees the garden as a chance for a fresh start and a calm, low-maintenance sanctuary where she can unwind all year round. Her son Jacob, however, has a very different vision: he’s passionate about rewilding, keen to create hedgerows, natural habitats and a thriving space for wildlife. Maisie, meanwhile, just wants to make sure their two beloved cats have plenty to explore and enjoy. The family can’t agree on how to bring these distinct ideas together, and that’s where Chris and Flo step in. Louise also hopes to reuse old materials already in the garden, including weathered pallets, to keep the project sustainable and environmentally friendly. Can the team find the perfect balance between rewilding and relaxation, and create a beautiful garden that finally brings this family together all on a £3,000 budget?

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Beans?! New presenter Rob Bent is stunned by Rupert's quirky plan to cover a kitchen unit in baked-bean tins, but will buyers bite or leave it on the shelf? Upcycling sisters Katie and Sophie have a plan to make a dated dresser and drawers reflect their own personalities, and Rob hopes to make a vanity mirror reflect a profit.

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: David follows the house from the poverty-stricken 1930s through the Second World War and the cultural renaissance of postwar Edinburgh, all the way to the present day. The episode follows the Ruggs, who were witnesses to the first German attack on mainland Britain, in October 1939; the Shiels family, whose grandchildren show David a treasure trove of family letters and recall the destruction of the nearby slums; architect Alex Brown, who bought number 22 out of disbelief that the beautiful Georgian house could be threatened; and banjo player JJ Jamieson, who was attached to the city's cultural vibrancy. Finally, David invites present-day residents Morag and Henrietta to hear about their predecessors in the house. Who will win the bet about how the house was originally built, and what will Henrietta make of number 20 once being run as a brothel?

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Abbey Clancy and Peter Crouch present an appeal on behalf of Variety, the Children's Charity, which provides life-changing practical support for disabled and disadvantaged children and young people across the UK.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Angela Barnes, Kemah Bob, Ade Edmondson and Beattie Edmondson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the House of Games golden goblets, or will they be tempted by the branded golden fondue set?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek Brockway scours the archives for another three walks from around Wales. In Powys, he is cycling around the beautiful Lake Vyrnwy with fellow weather presenter Sian Lloyd. They learn about the village that was flooded to make way for the reservoir which still supplies Liverpool with water, and marvel at the famous dam, a Victorian engineering feat. For his second walk, Derek is in Eryri National Park to walk a section of the Slate Trail, created to promote the former slate-mining communities in the area. The route takes him from Capel Curig, where he has a go at rock climbing, via the stunning Swallow Falls, to picturesque Betws-y-Coed, where he is given a lesson in charcoal drawing. For his final walk, Derek takes a hike with a difference - his partners are a pair of llamas! Together they explore the beautiful Berwyn Mountains in north east Wales.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben Fogle and Kate Humble are back for another sunny summer series, following the remarkable lives of the exotic animals at Longleat Safari Park, and the keepers who care for their every need. We see the many ways the keepers of the park go above and beyond to keep all their animals healthy and happy. The keepers have to carry out essential health checks on the park’s new red pandas. The animals spend most of their lives in the treetops, so it’s hard to see their feet, but the park has a plan. They’re building a clever gadget, which will show a red panda’s reflection, but only if the red pandas can be persuaded to stand on it. How will the keepers encourage these famously nervous animals to come near it? Elsewhere in the park, Kate helps with the keepers' plans for a lads' day out for the lions. They’re putting one of the prides into another lion’s territory in an attempt to analyse the current pride structure. Megan helps the keepers give an Argentine tegu a bath, and Hamza has been given a challenge to film one of the park’s rhino horns very close up – an easy job when the subject is still, something the rhinos rarely are.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Singer-songwriter and talent show judge Pixie Lott hopes to confirm a family story that she has Italian ancestry from Verona, but instead discovers ancestors battling poverty and hardship in London. On her dad’s side, Pixie learns of her great-grandfather’s harrowing and surprising experience in the First World War. And wondering if she has any musical genes, Pixie is delighted to discover three generations of military musicians, whose legacy gives her an opportunity to sing with the band of the Household Cavalry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team of experts bring this edition from the Royal Hospital at Haslar in Gosport. The featured items include a satinwood secretaire known as Aunt Selina, a radiograph of Edward VIII's hand, an Edward Lear sketch, a gold painted bronze, a Steiff teddy, and ceremonial silverware given by Tsar Nicolas II to HMS Lion.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: From the splendid interior of Gloucester Cathedral, presenter Paul Martin, along with experts Catherine Southon and Philip Serrell, views some exceptional items brought in for valuation. The items selected for auction range from a set of Victorian jelly moulds to an exquisite French snuff box. Paul also finds out more about the brief, but intense, friendship between poets Edward Thomas and Robert Frost whilst they were living in the Gloucestershire countryside just before World War I.

programme.title: Athletics: The Ultimate Championship
programme.desc: Live coverage from Budapest of day 1 of the inaugural edition of the World Athletics Ultimate Championship.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: After a summer of heat and drought, Adam Frost shares some timely advice on how to capture rainwater. He also gives a practical guide to laying paving and comes up with a cunning plan on how to use prolific self-seeders. Sue Kent is at home planting Swiss chard and shows how to tackle an outbreak of fuchsia gall mite, while Frances Tophill visits a garden in Somerset whose owners take inspiration from the surrounding landscape. There are two friends who have a passion for producing organic, open-pollinated seed on a flower-filled farm in Devon. Plus a couple in Saltdean who have created a beautiful retreat high up on the rolling South Downs.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The magnificent Sara Pascoe introduces comedians Amy Gledhill and Eddie Kadi to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight

programme.title: Club Zero
programme.desc: Ms Novak joins the staff of an international boarding school to instruct a 'conscious eating' class. She teaches that eating less is healthy. The other teachers are slow to notice what is happening, and by the time the distracted parents begin to realise, Club Zero has become a reality.

programme.title: Golf: Solheim Cup
programme.desc: The opening day of the 2026 Solheim Cup as Europe take on the United States, with the event being played in the Netherlands for the first time. Europe are looking to win the trophy back on home soil after Team USA secured victory in the biennial contest for the first time since 2017 two years ago. Eight points are up for grabs on day one, with four morning foursomes matches followed by four afternoon fourballs. Sweden’s Anna Nordqvist captains Team Europe, with the USA led by Angela Stanford.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 3 highlights from the third Test match between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Twenty-five years after the 9/11 attacks killed almost 3,000 people, tens of thousands of newly released documents are shedding fresh light on the claim that individuals working for the Saudi government might have been involved. Panorama investigates the role of Omar al-Bayoumi, who helped the first two hijackers after they arrived in America. A US judge has found that he could have been an agent working on the instructions of the Saudi government – something he, and Saudi Arabia, have always denied. After being arrested by British police and held for seven days, al-Bayoumi was released and allowed to return to Saudi Arabia. But Jane McMullen, reporting for Panorama, explores whether UK officers and FBI agents had access to all the available evidence against him. She uncovers never-before-broadcast video footage, hears from people close to the case who have never spoken before and asks why significant evidence remained hidden for so long.

Sue Kent is at home planting Swiss chard and shows how to tackle an outbreak of fuchsia gall mite, while Frances Tophill visits a garden in Somerset whose owners take inspiration from the surrounding landscape. programme.title: The Red Shoes
programme.desc: Eager young ballerina Victoria Page is delighted at being given the opportunity to dance with the renowned Ballet Lermontov, little realising the demands of its brilliant yet arrogant impresario will force a tragic choice between her career and her lover.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the semi-final, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young set three challenges celebrating wardrobe heroes. These are items found in every wardrobe. However little or often they are worn, these clothes are must-haves and essentials. First, in the Pattern Challenge, the sewers must put their spin on the classic leather jacket, only this time, the judges have asked them to use plant-based leather. Next, for the Transformation Challenge, the sewers take men’s shirts and transform them into outfits for a wedding. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, it’s the timeless little black dress that is the inspiration. Four sewers remain, but only three will make it to the final.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Five fearless teams hit the windswept shores of St Andrews for Monster Day, battling six hours of gale-force winds and the creeping tide to carve their most gruesome creations yet. There are devilish beasts, twisted clowns and something jaw-dropping as imagination and creativity meet pure endurance. Will these towering terrors stand tall or crumble into the sea? One team will claim Sand Champion glory, and for one, it’s game over when the tide rolls in. Who will survive this beach of horrors?

programme.title: Lawrence of Arabia
programme.desc: Leaving his station in Cairo, the idealistic, misfit First World War British officer TE Lawrence begins an ambitious movement against the Turks by uniting warring tribes and becomes a legend.

programme.title: Athletics: The Ultimate Championship
programme.desc: Live coverage from Budapest of day 2 of the inaugural edition of the World Athletics Ultimate Championship.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! has come to Aberystwyth and the Old College, the original site of the first university in Wales. The experts on duty are David Harper and Christina Trevanion. Christina values a Victorian claret jug, and David gets all of a flutter over a large selection of antiques fans. Meanwhile, Paul Martin visits Laugharne, the home of his literary hero Dylan Thomas.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: In the first programme of the series, Paul visits Wester Ross and discovers the heritage of Little Loch Broom. He then travels to the off-grid community of Scoraig where he learns about violin making and wind power, before taking the plunge to explore the hidden depths of the Corrieshalloch Gorge. In Ullapool, on the shores of Loch Broom, Paul learns the Russian word for parsley and how a huge fleet of Russian fish factory ships known as Klondykers used to visit the town. He then follows a red herring that connects the lochs of the west coast to the history of the slave trade. Journey’s end is on the rocky summit of Stac Pollaidh.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Katie Derham and Nick Mohammed lead the celebrations live from the Royal Albert Hall as the biggest party in classical music gets under way. Superstar pianist Yuja Wang and operatic sensation Nicky Spence top the bill as Sakari Oramo conducts the BBC Symphony Orchestra and Chorus, and the BBC Singers. Highlights include Bernstein’s sparkling Overture to Candide, Barber’s Piano Concerto and Smetana’s epic Má vlast.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: Highlights from a packed first day of incredible music at Radio 2 in the Park in Stirling, featuring standout performances from Texas, Lulu, Jack Savoretti, ABC, The Script and Emeli Sandé as a spectacular day of live music is celebrated in Scotland.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: The 'queen of funk’, Chaka Khan, headlines the first day of Radio 2 in the Park live from Stirling, bringing her powerhouse vocals, legendary hits and five decades worth of soul and funk to the stage. Join the global superstar for an unforgettable headline performance packed with classic songs, incredible energy and the unmistakable voice that has made her a music icon.

programme.title: Chaka Khan at the BBC
programme.desc: Ain’t Nobody quite like Chaka Khan, and the proof of that comes courtesy of the BBC’s music archives, which have been plundered for this celebration of one of the all-time great queens of soul. This selection of Chaka’s finest BBC moments covers five decades of performing, reflecting a career that started in the 70s with her partnership with Rufus and eventually led to the massive number one hit I Feel for You, which helped bring rap right into the mainstream, and I’m Every Woman, an instant anthem that made her a lifelong female icon.

programme.title: Texas at the BBC
programme.desc: Sharleen Spiteri takes a dive into the BBC’s music archives for a look back at some of Texas’s greatest appearances on a selection of programmes and live events from across their 35-year career. It’s a collection featuring all the band’s biggest hits, from I Don’t Want a Lover and Black Eyed Boy to Summer Son and Say What You Want, combined with Sharleen’s memories of several of her own favourite moments, including 2023’s triumphant return to the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury, dressing up as Elvis and a key collaboration with hip-hop icons Wu-Tang Clan. For fans, this collection shows exactly how Texas rose to become one of Scotland’s finest groups and demonstrates how they’ve managed to stay on top for so long.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 4 highlights from the third Test match between England and Pakistan at Edgbaston.

programme.title: Saint Omer
programme.desc: Pregnant young novelist Rama attends the trial of Laurence Coly, a Senegalese woman accused of murdering her 15-month-old child by leaving her on a beach to be swept away. In French and Wolof with English subtitles

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Anita Rani are in Cumbria to see how arable farmers more used to rain than drought have fared after a record-breaking dry summer. John visits a farm in the south of the county that is sticking with a crop dependent on wet weather, despite a failed harvest. In the north east of the county, Anita discovers how one family has turned to a heritage grain that could help secure its future. Adam Henson sees how the hot weather has affected his livestock, and the Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need is back this autumn! To kick things off, John is joined by Matt Baker and Pudsey to introduce the first of a group of children supported by projects funded by the charity.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek follows the River Taff to Breacon, stands on Devil’s Bridge in Pontarfynach and takes the steam train around Barmouth Bay, as he revisits his most loved waterways walks.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: As autumn approaches, it’s time to look at the seasons to come. Brian Cunningham launches an experiment to compare the performance of something planted now with the same variety held over and not planted until spring. Ruth Vichos looks back at two of the projects she has been overseeing this summer - her vertical garden, which is ideal for those who don’t have much space to grow, and the strawberry bed that was started three years ago by Carole Baxter, and which now needs to be refreshed. Brian also looks at end-of-summer lawn care after months of mixed conditions, though it has not been as dry at Beechgrove as elsewhere in the country. There is a final visit to Colin Crosbie’s plot just outside Dumfries, and we find out if Jenna McDonald, who was growing flowers on her Perth allotment for her own wedding, has been successful.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt shares an abundance of autumnal recipes from the Saturday Kitchen archives. Elliott Grover has a twist on pork belly, roasting it until the skin becomes crackly and crisp before serving it with herb-roasted potatoes, charred cabbage and a strawberry and cider sauce. Theo Randall celebrates the best of the season's produce with his fennel and porcini steamed sea bass with wilted rainbow chard and a rich vermouth butter sauce. Tony Singh demonstrates how to make a samosa with three sauces, including tamarind chutney and mint chutney. Anthony Murphy delivers a masterclass in making the perfect cheeseburger. And Romesh Ranganathan tucks into either his food heaven, passion fruit and mango millefeuille, or his food hell, a Lyonnaise lentil salad. Meanwhile, Rick Stein celebrates his love of frozen peas, and the Hairy Bikers cook up a Corsican breakfast.

programme.title: Caribbean Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Levi Roots tempts shoppers in Glasgow with an aromatic pineapple dessert, takes to the seas to show Mull fishermen how to dub up their catch, and lays on the ultimate Caribbean cricket tea for two teams of hungry Yorkshiremen.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. In this episode she helps Sonia Harwood, a mother of three and foster carer, who would love to create homemade family meals but ends up relying on frozen food. Lorraine shows her how easy cooking with fresh ingredients can be, demonstrating recipes including courgette fritters, a quick seafood linguine and an impressive baked ricotta cheesecake.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The reds and blues are bargain hunting at the Mona Showground on the Isle of Anglesey in north Wales. Anita Manning is overseeing proceedings, and experts Danny Sebastian and Nick Hall help the teams invest their £300 wisely. Meanwhile, Anita pays a visit to a local jewellery maker to find out more about amber.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: Four pairs of aspiring art dealers remain to compete in the semi-final, and all of them have their eyes on the ultimate prize of £50,000 worth of British art. To take them one step closer, host Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas welcome them onboard the luxurious Queen Anne cruise ship, where they’ll spend three days at sea, working to a specific brief and stepping into the world of art curation. Joined by guest mentors and curators Wilhelm Finger and Melita Skamnaki, the pairs are once again split into teams before being tasked with curating a collection of art fit for the ship’s newest cabaret bar. One team secures a lucrative deal, while one pair faces elimination.

programme.title: Women's Super League

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Ashridge House in Hertfordshire, where hundreds of people arrive with their antiques and collectibles. The experts find interesting objects to take to auction, and Paul Martin learns about the work of a famous local sculptor – Sir Henry Moore.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Eagles are the most powerful birds in the sky. They are capable of tackling enormous prey, spotting food at vast distances and soaring for miles on the wing. But how do they achieve this? To find out, this film follows the dramatic story of a family of bald eagles, and bird specialist Lloyd Buck puts his trained golden eagle to the test in a series of remarkable experiments.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at one of the estate's most valuable yet vulnerable crops, blueberries, and meets the estate owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team as they work to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife. He also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the estate's farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims travel from Appenzell to their final destination at Einsiedeln Abbey. They witness a lively cattle show in Urnasch, learn about the Jewish heritage of two Swiss villages, and tackle a muddy and steep path through the mountains as the weather deteriorates further. Finally, they reach the abbey's beautiful 10th-century church, with its famed Black Madonna in the Chapel of Mercy.

programme.title: Rob and Rylan's Passage to India
programme.desc: Rob and Rylan are on the final leg of their Indian adventure. They’re bound for Varanasi, the spiritual heart of India, where millions come to wash away their sins before they die. But first, the boys head to the famous erotic temples of Khajuraho - ancient structures covered in carvings depicting all kinds of carnal pleasure. In Varanasi, they drift down the sacred Ganges, witnessing pilgrims chasing ‘moksha’ - liberation from reincarnation. They join a mud-wrestling club inspired by Hanuman, the monkey god of strength. There are other kinds of spiritual journey available in the city. A guru tells Rob he must walk barefoot through the town, dodging cow dung and existential dread as he goes. Rylan, meanwhile, is told he must find a path to enlightenment through yoga.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: Highlights from a packed final day of incredible music at Radio 2 in the Park in Stirling, featuring standout performances from Deacon Blue, Appleton, Blue, Cast, James Blunt and Level 42 for a spectacular day of live music in Scotland.

programme.title: Golf: Solheim Cup
programme.desc: Highlights from the final day singles at the 2026 Solheim Cup as the contest between Europe and the United States reaches its conclusion. The 20th edition of the biennial contest is being played in the Netherlands for the first time, with Europe looking to win the trophy back on home soil after Team USA secured victory for the first time since 2017 two years ago. Twelve singles matches take place on day three, with the competition having reached nerve-shredding and dramatic climaxes on several occasions down the years – including a 14-14 draw the last time it was played in Europe, in 2023. Sweden’s Anna Nordqvist captain’s Team Europe, with Team USA led by Angela Stanford.

programme.title: One Zoo Three
programme.desc: Cam, Tyler and Aaron explore the wonders of the wetlands and meet the wildlife heroes working hard to help protect its animal inhabitants. It’s an early start for Tyler as he heads to Devon hoping to bump into a beaver and discover why this furry eco engineer is having a huge impact on the land and its wildlife. Cam is on the outskirts of Manchester to lend a hand restoring a wetland habitat that is helping combat climate change, all thanks to a super-plant called sphagnum moss. On the Isle of Mull, the OZT brothers go head-to-head as they look to spot an otter. They find out how this wetland wonder is making a big comeback - but whose animal tracking skills will win the day? Back at OZT HQ, a mini murmuration of starlings is flying around, and Aaron is ready with some starling statistics, but he has the crowd guessing when it comes to playing Fact or Fake. Cam reveals an incredible scene from Sir David Attenborough’s Wild Isles and gives Tyler a real soaking as he demonstrates how they might film similar shots using a super slo-mo camera. And the brothers find out what has been going wild near you, in the OZT Gallery.

programme.title: Planet Defenders
programme.desc: Environmentalist Jack has made films since he was very young and has a loyal following online. More recently he has thrown himself into climate change activism and working to increase awareness of the threats to our planet. His mission is to investigate the growing but sometimes controversial movement to rewild Britain. Jack discovers how the first legalised reintroduction of the beaver to England is having dramatic results. It is re-engineering river systems and creating rich habitats for many other species. He learns that despite the benefits of having this giant rodent around, some people think bringing it back is bad news. Jack travels to the Highlands of Scotland to witness the beauty of a 300-acre area of land that has been allowed to regenerate in its natural way for the past 40 years. It is here that he comes face to face with endangered wildlife such as red squirrels and pine martens, that have crept back from the brink of extinction to live in this wilderness. He also learns about a vision of the future to reintroduce one of Britain’s most elusive and special predators: the wildcat.

programme.desc: A musician couple captures a sound not meant for human ears. Soon, a stranger knocks on their door and their reality begins to blur.

programme.title: Mr. Nobody (Extended Director's Cut)
programme.desc: Mr. Nobody tells the life story of Nemo Nobody, a 118-year-old man who is the last mortal on Earth after the human race has achieved quasi-immortality.

programme.title: The Last Days on Mars
programme.desc: On the eve that the crew of the very first manned expedition to Mars is about to return to Earth, it makes an astounding discovery - fossilized evidence of life on Mars.
A man's life is derailed when a pattern of events repeats itself at exactly 2:22pm every day.

programme.title: High-Rise
programme.desc: Tom Hiddleston stars as Dr. Robert Laing, the newest resident of a luxurious apartment in a high-tech skyscraper whose lofty location places him amongst society's upper class.

programme.title: Skin Trade
programme.desc: With nothing but vengeance to live for, detective Nick Cassidy ransacks his way through the Bangkok underworld in pursuit of Viktor Dragovic, the human trafficker who killed his family.

programme.title: The Canyon
programme.desc: Honeymooners Nick and Lori head off to the Grand Canyon for adventure and time alone together.

programme.title: The Sacrament
programme.desc: A mysterious rural utopia quickly becomes evident that this paradise may not be as it seems.

programme.title: Alone
programme.desc: A grief-stricken young widow flees the city to cope with the loss of her husband. When she's kidnapped by a man and locked in a cabin, she escapes into the wilderness and is pursued by her captor.

programme.title: The Hunter
programme.desc: Willem Dafoe plays a mercenary sent by a corporation to the untamed wilderness of Tasmania to track down a tiger thought to be extinct, whose genetic code holds the secret to a dangerous weapon.

programme.title: Deadfall
programme.desc: Siblings Addison (Eric Bana) and Liza (Olivia Wilde) are fleeing from a casino heist when their getaway results in a car accident and a dead state trooper.

programme.title: Kingsman: The Golden Circle
programme.desc: With their headquarters destroyed and the world held hostage, members of Kingsman find new allies when they discover a spy organization in the United States known as Statesman. In an adventure that tests their strength and wits, the elite secret agents from both sides of the pond band together to battle a ruthless enemy and save the day, something that's becoming a bit of a habit for Eggsy.

programme.title: Red Sparrow
programme.desc: Prima ballerina Dominika Egorova faces a bleak and uncertain future after she suffers an injury that ends her career. She soon turns to Sparrow School, a secret intelligence service that trains exceptional young people to use their minds and bodies as weapons. Egorova emerges as the most dangerous Sparrow after completing the sadistic training process. As she comes to terms with her new abilities, Dominika meets a CIA agent who tries to convince her that he is the only person she can trust.

programme.title: The Watchers
programme.desc: A 28-year-old artist gets stranded in an expansive, untouched forest in western Ireland. Finding shelter, she unknowingly becomes trapped alongside three strangers who are stalked by mysterious creatures every night.

programme.title: Blood Father
programme.desc: An ex-convict (Mel Gibson) and his estranged daughter (Erin Moriarty) go on the run from her drug-dealing boyfriend (Diego Luna) and his vicious cartel.

programme.title: Fantastic Beasts: A Natural History
programme.desc: Delving into the mythological, including dragons, mermaids, and unicorns -- alongside examinations of natural world beasts, such as vervet monkeys, narwhals, and manatees; Stephen Fry travels far and wide to learn about such animals.

programme.title: Monster-in-Law
programme.desc: Charlotte (Jennifer Lopez) is smitten when she meets Dr. Kevin Fields (Michael Vartan). So when Kevin pops the question after they start dating, Charlotte happily accepts. But she soon realizes that Kevin's mom, Viola (Jane Fonda), is not quite thrilled to have a new family member. Viola, a newscaster, has just lost her job and is feeling rather attached to Kevin, so she regards Charlotte as her new competition -- and will apparently do anything to make her son call off the wedding.

programme.title: Pacific Rim Uprising
programme.desc: Jake Pentecost is a once-promising Jaeger pilot whose legendary father gave his life to secure humanity's victory against the monstrous Kaiju. Jake has since abandoned his training only to become caught up in a criminal underworld. But when an even more unstoppable threat is unleashed to tear through cities and bring the world to its knees, Jake is given one last chance by his estranged sister, Mako Mori, to live up to his father's legacy.

programme.title: The Usual Suspects
programme.desc: "The greatest trick the devil ever pulled was convincing the world he didn't exist," says con man Kint, drawing a comparison to the most enigmatic criminal of all time, Keyser Söze. Kint attempts to convince the feds that the mythic crime lord not only exists, but is also responsible for drawing Kint and his four partners into a multi-million dollar heist that ended with an explosion in San Pedro Harbor - leaving few survivors.

programme.title: Aniara
programme.desc: When a spacecraft carrying settlers to Mars strays off course, the consumption-obsessed passengers are prompted to consider their place in the universe.

programme.title: My Soul to Take
programme.desc: In the small town of Riverton, a local legend tells of a serial killer's oath to come back and kill the seven children who were born on the night he supposedly died. Now 16 years later, Riverton residents are disappearing again, making some wonder if the legend is true. Bug (Max Thieriot), plagued by nightmares all his life, is one of the so-called Riverton Seven, and it's up to him to save his friends from an evil that will not rest.

programme.title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
programme.desc: On an empty road in the middle of the night, Shula stumbles across the body of her uncle. As the funeral unfolds, the cousins unveil the buried secrets of their Zambian family in a vibrant reckoning with the lies we tell ourselves.

programme.title: Just Friends
programme.desc: High school student Chris Brander (Ryan Reynolds) loves his best friend, Jamie Palamino (Amy Smart). He finally confesses his feelings, but she tells him that she just wants to be friends, and he leaves town in shame. Ten years later, Chris is a successful record executive and involved with self-absorbed pop star Samantha James (Anna Faris). He still pines for Jamie, though, and when his plans to go to Paris for the holidays fall through, he returns to his hometown to try and win her heart.

programme.title: Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
programme.desc: It's open season on Harley Quinn when her explosive breakup with the Joker puts a big fat target on her back. Unprotected and on the run, Quinn faces the wrath of narcissistic crime boss Black Mask, his right-hand man, Victor Zsasz, and every other thug in the city. But things soon even out for Harley when she becomes unexpected allies with three deadly women -- Huntress, Black Canary and Renee Montoya.

programme.title: The Lobster
programme.desc: In a dystopian society, single people must find a mate within 45 days or be transformed into an animal of their choice.

programme.title: The Shape of Water
programme.desc: Elisa is a mute, isolated woman who works in a hidden, high-security government laboratory. Her life changes forever when she discovers the lab's classified secret -- a mysterious, scaled creature from South America that lives in a water tank.

programme.title: The Greatest Showman
programme.desc: Growing up in the early 1800s, P.T. Barnum displays a natural talent for publicity and promotion, selling lottery tickets by age 12. After trying his hands at various jobs, P.T. turns to show business to indulge his limitless imagination, rising from nothing to create the Barnum & Bailey circus. Featuring catchy musical numbers, exotic performers and daring acrobatic feats, Barnum's mesmerizing spectacle soon takes the world by storm to become the greatest show on Earth.

programme.title: Joker
programme.desc: Forever alone in a crowd, failed comedian Arthur Fleck seeks connection as he walks the streets of Gotham City. Arthur wears two masks -- the one he paints for his day job as a clown, and the guise he projects in a futile attempt to feel like he's part of the world around him. Isolated, bullied and disregarded by society, Fleck begins a slow descent into madness as he transforms into the criminal mastermind known as the Joker.

programme.title: Joker: Folie à Deux
programme.desc: Struggling with his dual identity, failed comedian Arthur Fleck stumbles upon true love while incarcerated at Arkham State Hospital. Awaiting trial for the murder of five people, Fleck soon discovers the music that's always been inside him.

programme.title: I Love You Forever
programme.desc: Following a young woman into and out of an emotionally abusive relationship.

programme.title: Dim Sum Funeral
programme.desc: In the wake of her death, the embittered children of Chinese-American matriarch Mrs. Xiao (Lisa Lu) begrudgingly return to their childhood home for a bristly -- and brief, they hope -- reunion. But after Xiao's maid and sole confidant, Viola (Talia Shire), reveals her wish to undergo a week-long Buddhist funeral rite, the younger Xiaos -- including plastic surgeon Alexander (Russell Wong) and lesbian actress Meimei (Steph Song) -- have seven days to come to terms with her death, and each other.

programme.title: The Judge
programme.desc: Hank Palmer (Robert Downey Jr.), a brilliant but shady attorney, returns to his Indiana hometown after learning that his mother has passed away. His arrival triggers renewed tension between himself and his father, Judge Joseph Palmer (Robert Duvall), who makes no secret of his disapproval of Hank's morally ambiguous career. As the lawyer prepares to depart, his father is arrested for a hit-and-run death. Hank takes on his father's defense, despite the objections of the resentful old man.

programme.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
programme.desc: In 1770 the young daughter of a French countess develops a mutual attraction to the female artist commissioned to paint her wedding portrait.

programme.title: Women Is Losers
programme.desc: Celina Guerrero attempts to rise above poverty in the 1960s San Francisco.

programme.title: Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga
programme.desc: Young Furiosa gets caught in the crossfire of two tyrannical warlords. As the tyrants fight for dominance, Furiosa soon finds herself in a nonstop battle to make her way home.

programme.title: Eyes Wide Shut
programme.desc: After Dr. Bill Hartford's (Tom Cruise) wife, Alice (Nicole Kidman), admits to having sexual fantasies about a man she met, Bill becomes obsessed with having a sexual encounter. He discovers an underground sexual group and attends one of their meetings -- and quickly discovers that he is in over his head.

programme.title: Red Riding Hood
programme.desc: Young Valerie (Amanda Seyfried) feels torn between two men. She loves Peter, but her parents intend that she marry wealthy Henry. Valerie and Peter are going to run away together, but her sister is killed by a werewolf before they can put their plan into action. The villagers call on the help of Father Solomon (Gary Oldman), a famous monster hunter who warns that the beast takes human form by day. Then Valerie suspects that the werewolf is someone she loves.

programme.title: The Wolfman
programme.desc: Though absent from his ancestral home of Blackmoor for many years, aristocrat Lawrence Talbot returns to find his missing brother at the request of the latter's fiancée, Gwen. He learns that a creature has links to an ancient curse turning people into werewolves when the moon is full. To save the village and protect Gwen, he must slay the bloodthirsty beast, but he contends with a horrifying family legacy.

programme.title: The Apparition
programme.desc: Plagued by frightening occurrences in their home, Kelly (Ashley Greene) and Ben (Sebastian Stan) learn that a university's parapsychology experiment produced an entity that is now haunting them. The malevolent spirit feeds on fear and torments the couple no matter where they run. Desperate, Kelly and Ben turn to a paranormal researcher (Tom Felton), but even with his aid, it may already be too late to save themselves from the terrifying presence.

programme.title: The Possession
programme.desc: When their youngest daughter, Em (Natasha Calis), becomes strangely obsessed with an antique wooden box bought from a yard sale, parents Clyde (Jeffrey Dean Morgan) and Stephanie (Kyra Sedgwick) see little cause for alarm. However, Em becomes increasingly unstable, leading the couple to fear the presence of a malevolent force. To their horror, Clyde and Stephanie learn that the box contains a dybbuk, a dislocated spirit that inhabits -- and ultimately devours -- a human host.

programme.title: Open Water
programme.desc: Daniel (Daniel Travis) and Susan (Blanchard Ryan) embark on a tropical vacation with their scuba-diving certifications in tow. During a group dive, the two separate themselves from the others to dive a little deeper. An incorrect head-count suggests the entire group has returned, so the boat departs. When the pair surfaces, they make out a vessel in the distance, but it does not immediately set in that they have been left behind. With sharks lurking beneath, their survival chances grow smaller.

programme.title: A Clockwork Orange
programme.desc: In an England of the future, Alex and his "Droogs" spend their nights getting high at the Korova Milkbar before embarking on "a little of the old ultraviolence," while jauntily warbling "Singin' in the Rain." After he's jailed for bludgeoning the Cat Lady to death, Alex submits to behavior modification technique to earn his freedom; he's conditioned to abhor violence. Returned to the world defenseless, Alex becomes the victim of his prior victims.

programme.title: Queer
programme.desc: Lee, a solitary American in Mexico City, falls for a beautiful, elusive former soldier. Journeying together into the jungle, Lee sees, for the first time, the possibility of an intimate and infinite love.

programme.title: Man Down
programme.desc: When U.S. Marine Gabriel Drummer (Shia LaBeouf) returns from Afghanistan, he finds the place he once called home is no better than the battlefields he fought on overseas. Accompanied by his best friend, a hard-nosed Marine whose natural instinct is to shoot first and ask questions later, Gabriel searches desperately for his estranged son and his wife, leading to a suspect who has vital information about their location.

programme.title: Meg 2: The Trench
programme.desc: Jonas Taylor leads a research team on an exploratory dive into the deepest depths of the ocean. Their voyage spirals into chaos when a malevolent mining operation threatens their mission and forces them into a high-stakes battle for survival. Pitted against colossal, prehistoric sharks and relentless environmental plunderers, they must outrun, outsmart and outswim their merciless predators.

programme.title: Cocktail
programme.desc: Brian Flanagan (Tom Cruise) wants a high-paying marketing job, but needs a business degree first. Working as a bartender to pay for college, Flanagan is mentored by his veteran boss, Doug Coughlin (Bryan Brown). Together, their showy tricks and charisma command large crowds and tip payments -- until Flanagan and the cynical Coughlin have a falling out. Flanagan moves to Jamaica to raise enough money to open his own bar, where he falls in love with artist Jordan Mooney (Elisabeth Shue).

programme.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
programme.desc: Godzilla and the almighty Kong face a colossal threat hidden deep within the planet, challenging their very existence and the survival of the human race.

programme.title: Judy
programme.desc: Thirty years after starring in "The Wizard of Oz," beloved actress and singer Judy Garland arrives in London to perform sold-out shows at the Talk of the Town nightclub. While there, she reminisces with friends and fans and begins a whirlwind romance with musician Mickey Deans, her soon-to-be fifth husband.

programme.title: The Maltese Falcon
programme.desc: In this noir classic, detective Sam Spade (Humphrey Bogart) gets more than he bargained for when he takes a case brought to him by a beautiful but secretive woman (Mary Astor). As soon as Miss Wonderly shows up, trouble follows as Sam's partner is murdered and Sam is accosted by a man (Peter Lorre) demanding he locate a valuable statuette. Sam, entangled in a dangerous web of crime and intrigue, soon realizes he must find the one thing they all seem to want: the bejeweled Maltese falcon.

programme.title: Rain Man
programme.desc: When car dealer Charlie Babbitt (Tom Cruise) learns that his estranged father has died, he returns home to Cincinnati, where he discovers that he has an autistic older brother named Raymond (Dustin Hoffman) and that his father's $3 million fortune is being left to the mental institution in which Raymond lives. Motivated by his father's money, Charlie checks Raymond out of the facility in order to return with him to Los Angeles. The brothers' cross-country trip ends up changing both their lives.

programme.title: War for the Planet of the Apes
programme.desc: Caesar (Andy Serkis) and his apes are forced into a deadly conflict with an army of humans led by a ruthless colonel (Woody Harrelson). After the apes suffer unimaginable losses, Caesar wrestles with his darker instincts and begins his own mythic quest to avenge his kind. As the journey finally brings them face to face, Caesar and the colonel are pitted against each other in an epic battle that will determine the fate of both of their species and the future of the planet.

programme.title: Risky Business
programme.desc: Ecstatic when his parents leave on vacation for a few days, high school senior Joel Goodsen cuts loose with his best friend Miles. After an attempt at securing the services of a prostitute goes slightly awry, Joel hires gorgeous Lana for a night of delight. Stunned by the amount of Lana's "bill" the next morning, Joel grows frantic after he crashes his father's Porsche. In an effort to raise lots of money fast, a desperate Joel turns the house into a brothel.

programme.title: The Art of Getting By
programme.desc: George (Freddie Highmore) is a senior at a posh Manhattan prep school, but his disaffected attitude leaves little room for toeing the line. He'd rather doodle and read philosophy, and he strenuously avoids his parents (Rita Wilson, Sam Robards) whenever possible. Unfortunately, George's attitude is endangering his chances of graduating. Then he meets Sally (Emma Roberts). George finds himself falling in love with her, but an older artist (Michael Angarano) adds a complication to the mix.

programme.title: For All Mankind
programme.desc: Directed by Al Reinert and with music scored by Brian Eno, "For All Mankind" provides a testament to NASA's Apollo program of the 1960s and '70s. Composed of actual NASA footage of the missions and astronaut interviews, the documentary offers the viewpoint of the individuals who braved the remarkable journey to the moon and back. While compiling the material for the film, Reinert went through more than six million feet of film of these historic moments.

programme.title: Opus
programme.desc: A journalist is invited to the remote compound of a legendary pop star who mysteriously disappeared 30 years ago. Surrounded by the star's cult of sycophants, she gets caught in the middle of his twisted plan.

programme.title: Pan
programme.desc: Living a bleak existence at a London orphanage, 12-year-old Peter finds himself whisked away to the fantastical world of Neverland. Adventure awaits as he meets new friend James Hook and the warrior Tiger Lily. They must band together to save Neverland from the ruthless pirate Blackbeard.

programme.title: Leave No Trace
programme.desc: A father and daughter live a perfect but mysterious existence in Forest Park, a beautiful nature reserve near Portland, Ore., rarely making contact with the world. But when a small mistake tips them off to authorities, they are sent on an increasingly erratic journey in search of a place to call their own.

programme.title: Maze Runner: The Death Cure
programme.desc: Thomas leads some escaped Gladers on their final and most dangerous mission yet. To save their friends, they must break into the legendary Last City, a WCKD-controlled labyrinth that may turn out to be the deadliest maze of all. Anyone who makes it out alive will get answers to the questions that the Gladers have been asking since they arrived in the maze.

programme.title: King's Ransom
programme.desc: When the rich and arrogant Malcolm King (Anthony Anderson) informs his wife, Renee (Kellita Smith), that he plans to divorce her, she becomes intent on taking as much of his money as possible in the settlement. Malcolm devises a way to keep his fortune, but it involves staging his own kidnapping. Unfortunately for Malcolm, numerous people, including the scheming Corey (Jay Mohr), are already planning on abducting him, and there are various inept attempts to procure the wealthy man's money.

programme.title: Get Him to the Greek
programme.desc: An ambitious executive at a record company, Aaron Green (Jonah Hill) gets what looks like an easy assignment: He must escort British rock legend Aldous Snow (Russell Brand) to L.A.'s Greek Theatre for the first stop on a lucrative comeback-concert tour. Snow, however, has different plans. Learning his true love is in California, the rocker vows to win her back before starting the tour, forcing Aaron to pull out all the stops to get Snow on stage in time.

programme.title: A Thousand Words
programme.desc: Jack McCall (Eddie Murphy) is a selfish literary agent whose fast-talking ways allow him to close any deal. His next target is New Age guru Dr. Sinja (Cliff Curtis), but the savvy doctor sees right through Jack. A magical tree appears in Jack's yard, and, according to Dr. Sinja, the tree and Jack are connected; every time Jack says a word, a leaf falls from the tree. When the last leaf drops, Jack will die. With just a thousand leaves left, Jack must learn to curb his speech or he's a goner.

programme.title: The Transporter Refueled
programme.desc: Frank Martin is living a less perilous lifestyle, or so he thinks, transporting classified packages for questionable people. Things get complicated when femme fatale Anna and her three accomplices orchestrate a bank heist and the kidnapping of Frank's father. It's all part of a grand plan to take down the human trafficker who victimized her years earlier. Now a pawn in her vengeful scheme, the former special-operations mercenary must use his covert skills to play Anna's dangerous game.

programme.title: Judy
programme.desc: Thirty years after starring in "The Wizard of Oz," beloved actress and singer Judy Garland arrives in London to perform sold-out shows at the Talk of the Town nightclub. While there, she reminisces with friends and fans and begins a whirlwind romance with musician Mickey Deans, her soon-to-be fifth husband.

programme.title: Trap
programme.desc: A man and his teenage daughter realize they're at the center of a dark and sinister event while watching a concert.

programme.title: Scanners
programme.desc: Scanners are men and women born with incredible telepathic and telekinetic powers. There are many who exercise the benefits of their special gifts in a safe and judicious manner. However, there is a group of renegade scanners who plan to create a race that will rule the world.

programme.title: The Last Samurai
programme.desc: Capt. Nathan Algren (Tom Cruise) is an American military officer hired by the Emperor of Japan to train the country's first army in the art of modern warfare. As the government attempts to eradicate the ancient Samurai warrior class in preparation for more Westernized and trade-friendly policies, Algren finds himself unexpectedly affected by his encounters with the Samurai, which places him at the center of a struggle between two eras and two worlds.

programme.title: Beirut
programme.desc: In the 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working undercover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.

programme.title: Aftermath
programme.desc: Two strangers' lives become inextricably bound together after an error by an air traffic controller (Scoot McNairy) causes the death of a construction foreman's (Arnold Schwarzenegger) wife and daughter.

programme.title: Mojave
programme.desc: A down-and-out artist (Garrett Hedlund) has a dangerous and shocking encounter with an evil drifter (Oscar Isaac) in the desert, leading to terrifying consequences when the deadly stranger follows his unsuspecting victim home.

programme.title: Hitchcock
programme.desc: Following his great success with "North by Northwest," director Alfred Hitchcock makes a daring choice for his next project: an adaptation of Robert Bloch's novel "Psycho." When the studio refuses to back the picture, Hitchcock decides to pay for it himself in exchange for a percentage of the profits. His wife, Alma Reville, has serious reservations about the film but supports him nonetheless. Still, the production strains the couple's marriage.

programme.title: Show Dogs
programme.desc: After a failed attempt to recover a stolen baby panda, police dog Max reluctantly teams up with a human FBI agent named Frank. A hot tip leads Max and Frank to Las Vegas for the world's most exclusive dog show. To find the panda, Max goes undercover as a contestant to get the lowdown from his fellow canines. With help from their new friends, the crime-fighting duo must now foil another kidnapping plot and rescue other valuable animals from a gang of greedy smugglers.

programme.title: Robin Hood
programme.desc: After the death of Richard the Lion-Hearted, a skilled archer named Robin Longstride travels to Nottingham, where villagers suffer under a despotic sheriff and crippling taxation. He meets and falls in love with a spirited widow, Marion, although she is skeptical of his motives. Hoping to win her heart and save the village, Robin gathers a band of warriors to fight corruption in Nottingham, little knowing they will soon be fighting to save England itself.

programme.title: The Switch
programme.desc: Neurotic Wally Mars has one bright spot in his life: his friendship with Kassie. When Kassie announces her intention to become pregnant using a sperm donor, Wally thinks he will be the lucky guy, but Kassie has someone else in mind. While drunk at Kassie's insemination party, Wally substitutes his sperm for the donor's, then passes out, remembering nothing. Seven years later, Wally meets Kassie's son, who seems oddly familiar to him.

programme.title: Ricochet
programme.desc: After tracking down and arresting Earl Talbot Blake (John Lithgow), a psychotic hit man, rookie Los Angeles police officer Nick Styles (Denzel Washington) is hailed as a hero. Several years later, Styles' life appears perfect: He has married his girlfriend, started a family and risen to the position of assistant district attorney. However, his world is turned upside down when Blake escapes from prison with plans to exact brutal and well-calculated revenge.

programme.title: Inconceivable
programme.desc: Angela develops a friendship with a mysterious woman named Katie and offers her a job as a live-in nanny. The natural bond soon turns into a dangerous obsession as Katie becomes overly attached to the family's young daughter. Enduring lies and manipulations, Angela and her husband realize that sweet Katie is actually trying to destroy their family from within.

programme.title: The Flash
programme.desc: Worlds collide when the Flash uses his superpowers to travel back in time to change the events of the past. However, when his attempt to save his family inadvertently alters the future, he becomes trapped in a reality in which General Zod has returned, threatening annihilation. With no other superheroes to turn to, the Flash looks to coax a very different Batman out of retirement and rescue an imprisoned Kryptonian -- albeit not the one he's looking for.

programme.title: Magnolia
programme.desc: On one random day in the San Fernando Valley, a dying father, a young wife, a male caretaker, a famous lost son, a police officer in love, a boy genius, an ex-boy genius, a game show host and an estranged daughter will each become part of a dazzling multiplicity of plots, but one story.

programme.title: Lady Bird
programme.desc: A teenager (Saoirse Ronan) navigates a loving but turbulent relationship with her strong-willed mother (Laurie Metcalf) over the course of an eventful and poignant senior year of high school.

programme.title: Y2K
programme.desc: On the last night of 1999, two high school juniors crash a New Year's Eve party, only to find themselves fighting for their lives when the terror of Y2K becomes a reality and all machines rise up against humanity.

programme.title: Stonewall
programme.desc: Kicked out by his parents, a gay teenager (Jeremy Irvine) leaves small-town Indiana for New York's Greenwich Village, where growing discrimination against the LGBT community leads to riots on June 28, 1969.

programme.title: Brian Banks
programme.desc: The inspirational true story of Brian Banks, an all-American high school football star who finds his life upended when he's wrongly convicted of a crime he didn't commit. Despite the lack of evidence, Banks gets railroaded through a broken justice system and sentenced to a decade of prison and probation. Years later, with the support of Justin Brooks and the California Innocence Project, Banks fights to reclaim his life and fulfill his dreams of playing in the NFL.

programme.title: Fantastic Planet
programme.desc: This animated tale follows the relationship between the small human-like Oms and their much larger blue-skinned oppressors, the Draags, who rule the planet of Ygam. While the Draags have long kept Oms as illiterate pets, this hierarchy shifts after an Om boy becomes educated, thanks to a young female Draag. This leads to an Om rebellion, which weakens the Draag control over their race. Will the Oms and the Draags find a way to coexist? Or will they destroy each other?

programme.title: Hidden Figures
programme.desc: Three brilliant African American women at NASA, Katherine Johnson, Dorothy Vaughan and Mary Jackson, serve as the brains behind one of the greatest operations in history, the launch of astronaut John Glenn into orbit, a stunning achievement that restored the nation's confidence, turned around the Space Race and galvanized the world.

programme.title: Chasing Mavericks
programme.desc: When 15-year-old surfing phenomenon Jay Moriarty discovers that the mythic Mavericks surf break, one of the biggest waves on Earth, actually exists near his California home, he becomes determined to conquer it. Jay enlists the aid of local surfing legend Frosty Hesson to train him to ride the Mavericks and live to tell about it. As Jay and Frosty carry on their quest to achieve the impossible, they develop a unique friendship that transforms both their lives.

programme.title: Love, Simon
programme.desc: Everyone deserves a great love story, but for 17-year-old Simon Spier, it's a little more complicated. He hasn't told his family or friends that he's gay, and he doesn't know the identity of the anonymous classmate that he's fallen for online. Resolving both issues proves hilarious, terrifying and life-changing.

programme.title: Mississippi Masala
programme.desc: After Mina's Indian family is ousted from their home in Uganda by dictator Idi Amin, they relocate to Mississippi to start a new life. Mina falls for Demetrius, a young carpet cleaner, despite the protestations of their families over their racial difference. The families and their surrounding communities begin to feud, putting even more pressure on the couple's romance. Having to choose between family and love, Mina and Demetrius run away together.

programme.title: Mid90s
programme.desc: In the 1990s Los Angeles, a 13-year-old spends his summer navigating between a troubled home life and a crew of new friends he meets at a skate shop.

programme.title: The Player
programme.desc: Certain that the anonymous threats he's been receiving are the work of David Kahane (Vincent D'Onofrio), producer Griffin Mill (Tim Robbins) tries to fix things over cocktails. Instead, Griffin ends up murdering the screenwriter and courting the dead man's girlfriend (Greta Scacchi). As police investigate, Griffin concentrates on a prestigious film that might reinvigorate his career. But he soon learns that David's demise hasn't been forgotten by everyone in Hollywood.
